method: Fresh-context, label- and prediction-blind agent review of the supplied report texts and written guide only. Each category, urgency and clarification judgment was made individually using the reviewer's own judgment; no keyword classifier, existing model, repository material, original annotations, other reviews or evaluation results were used. Code was used only to read the two inputs, package the manually authored judgments and validate coverage and field types.
guide_notes: The guide does not explicitly distinguish an active unsafe destination from the urgent logistics blocker restoring its safety system. I applied safety precedence where unsafe personnel or rising floodwater are explicitly described (RLY-61963 and RLY-23213). I retained the missing or documentation cause for other blocked safety-system replacements without a separately described active physical event, while still marking them urgent.

The guide does not expressly say whether archival safety reports or cold-chain investigation and logger records become documentation cases. I used the underlying safety or temperature domain because documentation is specifically described through trade and delivery documents, and temperature records are expressly within temperature.

Routine means no immediate threat is described, while unclear urgency warns against treating missing information as proof of safety; the boundary is underspecified. I used routine for concrete operational incidents without an urgency cue, including some with unresolved identity or delivery records. I used unclear when reported cold-chain risk lacks the necessary temperature facts or an extremely vague report supplies no usable condition or consequence information.

The guide does not define how many facts must be missing before clarification is required. I did not flag normal recovery, claims, filing or tracing work by itself. I flagged explicit material gaps, conflicting accounts, unresolved primary issues, and separate active safety and transport handling.

There is no tie-breaker between packaging damage and a merely suspected shortage, or between a document discrepancy and the wrong consignment. I preserved an unclear primary category for RLY-95467 and RLY-94293 until inventory or actual consignment identity is verified.

Generic late again and everything is ruined statements could suggest delay or damage, but they do not establish the required shipment condition or specific primary issue. I used unclear for RLY-84412 and RLY-16564 rather than infer absent facts.

judgments.reason: The bag is located by a scan at a depot in the wrong city, so recovery is a transport delay. No immediate threat is described.
The subject is a safety near miss, but its review and corrective action are closed; only filing the final report remains.
This concerns temperature monitoring: two independent probes verified stable 5 C and the faulty sensor has been replaced. No continuing excursion is described.
Rain physically damaged the paper stock. The load is now in dry storage awaiting a claim inspection, with no ongoing hazard described.
Crushed lamp shades are the physical damage at issue, and the report expressly excludes smoke, leakage and a continuing hazard.
The apparel order disappeared between sorting hubs. There is no current evidence of a security incident or other immediate threat.
The splintered crate and chipped sculpture establish physical damage. The packing area has already been made safe.
The absent tariff heading requires a corrected declaration, making trade documentation the cause of the hold. No immediate threat is described.

Failed ventilation explicitly makes the destination unsafe for personnel, so the active unsafe condition takes precedence. Site safety and recovery of the delayed replacement motor need separate handling.
This is a completed evacuation exercise. The alarm was simulated and the report explicitly states there is no real emergency.
The claim concerns only a cosmetic packaging tear; the seal is intact and temperature records stayed in range.

The consignee lacks the container while the terminal records collection, leaving its delivery unconfirmed. The conflicting accounts and unidentified collecting vehicle need clarification; no immediate threat is described.

Refrigerated goods in an unpowered compartment create a cold-chain concern. Actual temperature, logger evidence and time without power are unavailable, so an uncontained excursion cannot be established or excluded.
Lithium cells are actively hissing and heating on an unisolated pallet with people close by, establishing an ongoing physical hazard.

Rising water and uncertain barrier endurance create an active safety threat while the emergency flood-protection pump is delayed. Barrier endurance is missing, and site protection and transport recovery need separate handling.
The mirror is fractured, but all pieces are secured in protective film and nobody is exposed.

The replacement module is unaccounted for and is needed now to restore failed emergency communications, meeting the critical-safety-system urgency rule. Its last carrying vehicle is an explicitly missing tracing fact.

The complaint concerns insufficient cooling, but measured temperature, required limits and transport records are all absent. Those facts are needed to judge whether an excursion exists and needs immediate action.
The defect is a blank proof-of-delivery signature file. The consignee confirms receipt of the undamaged shipment, so tracing or damage handling is not indicated.
Although the carton count is correct, the ordered instrument is absent from the sealed box. This is a missing-contents investigation with no immediate threat described.

Torn packaging is reported, but loss of contents is only suspected and no count or inventory is supplied. The primary issue cannot yet be separated into damage or missing contents; no immediate threat is described.
The request concerns the investigation of a cold-chain deviation. It is already isolated under a quality hold, and only investigation paperwork is requested.
The dented steel panel needs replacement approval. It is stable in the unloading area, with no continuing hazard described.
Unavailable receiving staff caused the destination to reschedule unloading, and the freight remains located on the vehicle. No immediate threat is described.
An uncontrolled liquid spill is spreading near a break area, creating an active unsafe condition. The liquid identity and hazard class are unknown and need clarification.
An armed threat is occurring beside the vehicle while the driver and cargo remain at the scene, requiring immediate security attention.
The manifest contains an outdated address, while the completed delivery was correct. The issue is record correction with no immediate cargo or safety threat described.
The intact shipment is located at the origin depot and missed departure because of a scheduling error. No immediate threat is described.
Freight required at minus 18 C is already at minus 2 C and continues warming without the refrigeration technician present, establishing an uncontained excursion.
A mandatory rest break makes arrival 90 minutes late. The ambient cargo is secure, and no immediate threat is described.
Ice cream is softening after compressor failure and remains without working cooling, so the temperature excursion is ongoing and uncontained.
The isolated phrase late again gives no shipment reference, item identity or account of its location or condition. The primary issue and any immediate consequences cannot be established.
Unsecured heavy crates are actively sliding toward the loading crew, creating an immediate physical hazard.
A worker is trapped beside a fallen load while vehicles continue moving through the area, establishing an ongoing danger to a person.
The invoice currency must be corrected before the customs entry is lodged. The report identifies no urgent use or cargo risk.

The buyer has no parcel and the photograph shows an unrecognised doorway, making delivery to the intended place unconfirmed. The exact delivery address needs confirmation; no immediate threat is described.
The receiver requests a stamped packing-list copy for accounts, and the report explicitly states there is no cargo operational issue.
The towel order is expected two hours late. ASAP and customer inconvenience do not establish urgency, and no service-critical impact is described.
Acid fumes are actively venting into an occupied warehouse and the area remains unisolated. This ongoing hazardous-substance exposure takes precedence over container damage.
Food cargo is warming rapidly after the cold-storage circuit tripped, and no spare cold room is available. The loss of temperature control is ongoing and uncontained.
The requested archive copy concerns a resolved access-security incident. The report explicitly excludes an ongoing intrusion.
All items were received, and the issue is the wrong company registration number on the electronic receipt.

The only replacement pressure-relief valve cannot be located, blocking restoration of the disabled site safety system. The missing shipment therefore meets the guide's urgent critical-system criterion.
The furniture delivery missed a preferred time slot. The report explicitly excludes damage, missing cargo and immediate risk.
A digit in the import permit number needs amendment. The goods are safe in the bonded facility, with no immediate threat described.
The warehouse received the return shipment but cannot now locate it, so shipment tracing is the primary task. No immediate threat is described.
An unsigned origin declaration prevents release, making trade documentation the operative cause. Storage conditions are satisfactory.
The request is for a temperature logger record for the quality archive. All recorded measurements met the shipment's storage conditions.
A cancelled ferry sailing delayed the located dry-goods load, and the customer agreed to delivery tomorrow. No immediate threat is described.
The warning concerns temperature monitoring, but it occurred on an empty return trip with no product on board.

The papers name machinery while the receiver expects clothing. Actual consignment identity is unverified, so the primary issue could be incorrect documents or a different shipment; no immediate threat is described.
A product requiring 2 to 8 C is now at 17 C after the vehicle was left open, and the consignment has not been quarantined. The reported excursion remains uncontained.
One fabric roll is unaccounted for after transfer. The report describes no incident or active hazard.

Everything is ruined does not establish the item, nature or extent of the alleged damage. Without details of the condition or any ongoing hazard, neither a primary category nor urgency can be established.
The printer housing is cracked, but the printer is unplugged and there are no exposed batteries or fluids. Physical damage is the main issue.
The books are located on the correct truck, but arrival will miss receiving-desk hours and requires a rebooked handover. No immediate threat is described.
The manifest has twelve units and the destination received eleven, establishing a one-unit shortage. The received units are intact and no immediate threat is described.
An unauthorised truck is actively removing goods from a locked compound, establishing an ongoing security incident requiring immediate assistance.

A clearance-document error blocks release of the replacement sprinkler controller. Because the destination has no working fire protection until it arrives, this documentation blocker meets the critical-safety-system urgency rule.
The bicycle frame is bent and has been set aside for a damage assessment. No continuing hazard is described.
